Part of the problem: 98 per cent of accounts hold less than VND 10 million
Payday Portfolio response: A payday standing order brings money in without a monthly decision
Evidence: Automatic enrolment raised participation from 37 to 86 per cent (Madrian & Shea, 2001)

Part of the problem: No product turns intention into regular deposits
Payday Portfolio response: Goal-based model portfolios through Ensa; rebalancing with new money
Evidence: 77 per cent of investors find portfolio management difficult (Section 2.7)

Part of the problem: Trust complaints deter the first deposit
Payday Portfolio response: Small, reversible transfers; no closure fee; one-screen terms; segregated-cash dashboard
Evidence: Trust complaints in 37 per cent of negative reviews, against 8 per cent at VPS (Section 2.6)

Part of the problem: Fewer than 2 in 100 accounts carry the platform's cost
Payday Portfolio response: Balances build in accounts already acquired; fee income needs no pledged borrowing
Evidence: Base case lifts accounts above VND 10 million to about 177,000 and cuts platform cost per funded account from VND 7.3 million to 1.1 million (Table F5)
